judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are Grade 3 Skills (rank 3, resolved coordinates). The second is Grade 3 / Term 3 / Writing / Shared, Group and Independent Writing: 'Summarises and records information using mind maps, tables, notices, diagrams or charts' (LCs: 'Records information using mind maps, tables, notices, diagrams or charts' and 'Summarises information using mind maps, tables, notices, diagrams or charts'). They are substantively coherent as complementary information-handling skills within the same grade year: one locates targeted information using a book's access features, the other condenses and re-represents information in written organisers, so they reinforce each other in information/research work. However, the second does not deepen, extend, or combine the first: it is a different capability in a different Skill Area, and the nomination evidence supporting any developmental link is lexical only (one shared token 'information', jaccard 0.05-0.10, trigram overlap generated by that same word, rank gap 0, shared Grade 3 banner ancestor). There is therefore no basis for asserting that proficiency with contents pages and indexes raises the likelihood of success at summarising into mind maps and charts, so the symmetric relatesTo is chosen over buildsTowards, and the relationship is more than generic repeated wording so no_relation is not appropriate. Confidence is moderated because both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted evidence items each) and several ancestors carry merge/audit context, including merged Term and Grade banner nodes.

judgment.rationale: Both Skills sit in Grade 1 (rank 1), Term 2, Reading and Phonics / Daily Phonemic Awareness-Phonic Activities, so the within-grade term ordering constraint is satisfied (same Term). The first statement is auditory discrimination of beginning and end sounds of words (LC tags: beginning sounds, end sounds, listening, phonemic awareness). The second requires actively building up and breaking down simple words into onset (initial sound) and rime and identifying rhymes (LC tags: blending, segmenting, onset, rime, rhyme). Hearing and distinguishing the initial sound versus the remainder of a word is the perceptual capability that makes onset-rime blending/segmentation and rhyme identification achievable, so proficiency in the first supports success in the more demanding manipulation skill; this is substantive extension (discrimination to manipulation/production), not mere repeated wording. Source evidence for both endpoints is truncated (24 omitted items each), but the printed bullets supplied are complete and sufficient; merge/audit context on both endpoints and all ancestors was inspected and shows routine singleton/merged banner decisions.

Shared tokens ('phonics', 'recognises', 'sounds'), the shared Grade 3 ancestor and rank-gap-0 proximity are nomination signals only and were not treated as progression evidence. Meaningful reinforcement without demonstrated dependency therefore supports symmetric relatesTo rather than buildsTowards. judgment.rationale: Both SFIs sit under Grade 3 (rank 3) Reading and Phonics, but in different terms and sub-strands: the first is Term 1 Phonics ('Recognises consonant digraphs (sh-, ch-, th-, wh-) at the beginning and end of words'), the second is Term 3 Group Guided Reading ('Monitors self when reading, both word recognition and comprehension'). Within the same grade the permitted developmental direction is earlier Term to same/later Term, so only first_to_second is semantically available here. Secure decoding of consonant digraphs in initial and final position gives learners the grapheme-phoneme knowledge needed to check and repair words during independent reading; the Term 3 statement explicitly names word recognition as one of the two strands being self-monitored, so Term 1 digraph proficiency plausibly supports success in self-monitoring. This is pair-specific decoding-to-self-monitoring support, not mere wording overlap (shared tokens are only 'and' plus the LC tags reading/word/recognition). Evidence limitation: both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted items each) and the second endpoint's LC metadata is truncated, so the full Term 3 context and the full Term 1 phonics bullet list were not inspected; the judgment rests on the printed statements, identity scopes and LC tags supplied.

judgment.rationale: Both are Grade 3, Term 4, WRITING, 'Shared, Group and Independent Writing' Skill bullets from the same source table row (page 132). First: 'Uses pre-writing strategies to gather information and plan writing: talks to a partner, creates a mind map, a planning frame'. Second: 'Builds own word bank and personal dictionary'. They are complementary writing-support practices — planning/organising content versus accumulating a personal vocabulary resource — and reinforce each other in composing texts, but neither statement's evidence indicates that proficiency in one is needed for or materially increases success in the other, and they sit at the same grade and term with no expansion of scope or independence in either direction. Shared ancestors, same-rank coordinate (Grade 3, rank 3), page proximity and the single shared LC tag 'writing' are nomination signals only, not developmental evidence. Symmetric conceptual coherence within the same sub-strand supports relatesTo. Source-evidence truncation on both endpoints and LC truncation on the second limit detail but do not alter this judgment.

judgment.rationale: Both Skills sit in Grade R (rank 0), Term 4, Skill Area Emergent Reading, but under different printed Sub-strands: 'Points at words rather than pictures when "reading"' falls under Shared Reading with LC tags print awareness/pointing/words, while 'Divides multisyllabic words into syllables: crocodile - croc-o-dile' falls under Phonological/Phonemic Awareness with LC tags phonological awareness/segmenting/syllables. They are complementary emergent-literacy strands that both develop awareness of the word as a unit (printed word in text vs spoken word segmented into syllables), which is substantive coherence rather than mere token overlap on 'words'. However, neither proficiency is evidenced as supporting success in the other: print-directionality/one-to-one pointing in shared reading and oral syllable segmentation are parallel, independently taught capabilities within the same term, and same-rank, same-Term placement supplies no developmental direction. Source evidence for both endpoints is truncated (24 omitted items each), so no stronger dependency claim is warranted; symmetric relatesTo is the supported judgment.

judgment.rationale: Both SFIs are Grade R Emergent Reading skills under the Phonological/Phonemic Awareness sub-strand (resolved Grade coordinate 'Grade R', rank 0 for both), so direction must rest on Term order within the grade. The second SFI sits under TERM 1 ('Can identify that oral sentences are made up of individual words: clap on each word in a sentence where all words have only one syllable'), while the first sits under TERM 4 ('Identifies rhyming words in well known rhymes and songs and in sequences of rhyming words'). This is not mere repeated wording: the Term 1 statement establishes conscious attention to spoken language as discrete word units (oral segmentation with clapping), which supports the later Term 4 demand of attending to and matching sound patterns within and across words in rhymes, songs and extended rhyming sequences. Shared LC tag 'phonological awareness' corroborates sub-strand coherence, and the permitted earlier-Term-to-later-Term direction (Term 1 -> Term 4, i.e. second_to_first) is the only valid developmental orientation here. Confidence is moderate because the two are partly parallel phonological-awareness sub-skills (word-level vs rhyme-level) rather than a strict prerequisite, and both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted source-evidence items each), so the full printed term bullets are not visible.

judgment.rationale: First endpoint: Grade 1 (rank 1), Term 2, WRITING / Handwriting — 'Writes words with correct spacing' (LC tags: handwriting, spacing, words, writing). Second endpoint: Grade 3 (rank 3), Term 2, WRITING / Shared, Group and Independent Writing — 'Writes and illustrates a story to contribute to a book for the class library' (LCs: writes a story for the class library; illustrates that story). Both sit in the WRITING Skill Area and are coherent as complementary aspects of producing hand-written text for readers: correctly spaced word-level handwriting is the production capability used when a child writes out and illustrates a story for the class library. That is meaningful, pair-specific instructional coherence rather than generic repetition, so relatesTo is warranted. buildsTowards is not warranted: the nomination rests on thin lexical/trigram overlap ('writes', 'writing'; jaccard 0.06-0.125), the two statements belong to different sub-strands that CAPS teaches concurrently (the Grade 3 Term 2 WRITING table context shows Handwriting continuing as its own sub-strand), and the Grade 3 demand is composition and illustration for an audience, not an extension or deepening of letter/word formation and spacing. relatesTo is symmetric, so direction is null and the canonical endpoint order is unchanged. Material limitations: both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted source-evidence items each) and the Grade/Term ancestors are merged banner nodes carrying audit context, so the full bullet context is not visible; confidence is held moderate accordingly.

judgment.rationale: First is Grade R / Term 2 / Emergent Reading / Emergent reading skills: 'Uses pictures to "read" simple phrase or caption books'. Second is Grade R / Term 3 / Emergent Writing / Emergent Writing: 'Contributes ideas for a class news book'. Both are Grade R (rank 0) emergent literacy skills centred on making meaning with books and picture-supported text, so they are mutually reinforcing complements across the reading and writing skill areas (picture-and-caption reading supports, and is supported by, co-constructing a class news book of pictures and dictated text). However, the evidence shows no substantive developmental dependency: contributing oral ideas to a shared class news book does not require, nor materially extend, the distinct capability of using pictures to 'read' caption books, and the only quantitative nomination signals are a shared Grade ancestor, zero rank gap, and trivial token overlap ('a', 'for', 'emergent', 'boo'/'ook'), which alone establish nothing. relatesTo therefore fits better than either buildsTowards direction. Both endpoints carry upstream merge/audit context and truncated source evidence (24 omitted evidence items each), so the full printed bullet context is only partially visible; this bounds but does not contradict the symmetric reading.

They are complementary components of independent written composition and reinforce one another, but neither statement expands, deepens or presupposes the other: correct tense use is not a stated condition for writing a poem or song, and poem/song writing does not extend tense control. With identical grade and term coordinates and no substantive evidence of developmental dependency, a buildsTowards in either direction is unsupported, so the symmetric relatesTo is the appropriate judgment. judgment.rationale: Both Skills are Grade 1 (rank 1), Term 4, Skill Area 'Reading and Phonics', but under different printed sub-strands: 'Group Guided Reading' (first) and 'Paired/Independent Reading (three times a week)' (second), rows 3 and 4 of the same Term 4 table. The first builds word-level recognition ('Continues to build a sight vocabulary from the incidental reading programme, the graded reading series and high-frequency word lists'); the second applies reading to whole familiar texts ('Reads books read in Shared Reading sessions and books from the classroom reading corner'). This is substantive, pair-specific coherence — automatic word recognition and independent/paired reading of familiar books mutually reinforce each other within the same weekly programme — so it is more than shared wording ('reading', 'and', 'from'), shared Skill Area, or source-page proximity. It does not, however, establish a developmental dependency in either direction: the two sub-strands are prescribed concurrently in the same Term of the same Grade, the sight-vocabulary bullet draws on a different word source (incidental programme, graded series, high-frequency lists) than the shared-reading/reading-corner books, and re-reading familiar books is itself a means of consolidating sight vocabulary, making the support reciprocal. With no stated expansion, extension, or increased complexity from one statement to the other, the configured same-grade/same-Term bar for buildsTowards is not met, so the symmetric relatesTo judgment is recorded with canonical endpoint order preserved and null direction. Evidence limitations: both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted items each) and the first endpoint's supporting LC evidence is truncated; both endpoints and all four shared ancestors carry upstream audit/merge context (ordinary Term/Grade banner merges and singleton sub-strand/bullet decisions), which is retained, not resolved.

judgment.rationale: Both Skills sit in Grade R (rank 0), Term 2, Skill Area 'Listening and Speaking (Oral)', but under different sub-strands: 'Daily activities in all areas of Language and other subjects' ('Listens to stories and acts these out') versus 'Uses visual and pictorial cues to make meaning' ('Orders a sequence of pictures and relates the story created'). Their LCs show genuine conceptual coherence around narrative — listening to stories and dramatising them (LCs 'Listens to stories', 'Acts out stories') complements sequencing pictures and orally relating the created story (LCs 'Sequences pictures', 'Relates the story created from the ordered pictures') — so they mutually reinforce story structure and oral expression. However, the two are concurrent Term 2 content with distinct modalities (aural/dramatic response vs visual sequencing and narration), and nothing in the bounded evidence shows one is a substantive precondition or extension of the other; same-rank, same-term placement alone cannot establish developmental direction, and the shared tokens ('and', 'oral', trigram fragments) are generic. Symmetric relatesTo is therefore the supported judgment. Note both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted items each) and several ancestors carry upstream merge/audit context, so the evidence base is bounded but not contradictory.

Direction is from the earlier Term 3 sentence-construction skill to the later Term 4 extended composition, which is permitted within a grade. Token/trigram overlap was only the generic 'such as' phrasing and was not used as evidence; the judgment rests on the shared Writing sub-strand, term ordering and the sentence-to-text progression. judgment.rationale: Both endpoints sit under Grade 2 (rank 2, resolved coordinates) in the Reading and Phonics skill area. The first is a Term 2 Phonics skill ('Recognises 'silent e'/split digraph in words For example tape, time, note'); the second is a Term 4 Group Guided Reading skill ('Reads silently and aloud from fiction and non-fiction books at own level in a guided reading group with teacher'), with LCs for silent reading and reading aloud of fiction/non-fiction at own level. Direction is from the earlier Term 2 phonics decoding skill to the later Term 4 connected-text reading, which is permitted within one grade. Decoding the split-digraph/'silent e' vowel pattern is a word-recognition capability that supports accurate decoding of the levelled fiction and non-fiction texts read aloud and silently in guided reading, so proficiency in the first plausibly supports success in the second. Note that the nomination's shared token 'silent' is coincidental ('silent e' versus 'reads silently') and was not treated as evidence; the judgment rests on the phonics-to-text-reading relationship, and both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted items each), which limits certainty, hence moderate confidence.
